question.worked_solution:
First, let's attempt to evaluate the limit by direct substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(2\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{\operatorname{sin}⁡0} \\  & =\frac{1}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

which is undefined.

Therefore, to find the limit, let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14258850/assets/eb99763da194e2e21ccb8032f049be9deb2f94605b70878968ccda1bc093c04c.png)

As $x$ approaches $0$ from the right, the values of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)$ are positive and grow without bound. Therefore

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x)=\infty .
$$
